sanskrit: dadarśātha tato jiṣṇuḥ puruṣaṃ kāñcanaprabham kirātaveṣapracchannaṃ strīsahāyam amitrahā tam abravīt prītamanāḥ kaunteyaḥ prahasann iva
english: Then Jiṣṇu (Arjuna), slayer of enemies, saw a man of golden radiance, disguised in the garb of a Kirata hunter and accompanied by women. The son of Kuntī, with a glad heart and as if laughing, addressed him.

sanskrit: ko bhavān aṭate śūnye vane strīgaṇasaṃvṛtaḥ na tvam asmin vane ghore bibheṣi kanakaprabha
english: "Who are you, wandering in this empty forest surrounded by a company of women? Do you feel no fear in this terrible forest, O man of golden radiance?"

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ ca tvayā viddho mṛgo 'yaṃ matparigrahaḥ mayābhipannaḥ pūrvaṃ hi rākṣaso 'yam ihāgataḥ
english: "And why have you shot this deer that was my quarry? I had pursued it first — for this was a rakshasa that came here in disguise."

sanskrit: kāmāt paribhavād vāpi na me jīvan vimokṣyase na hy eṣa mṛgayādharmo yas tvayādya kṛto mayi tena tvāṃ bhraṃśayiṣyāmi jīvitāt parvatāśraya
english: "Whether out of desire or out of contempt, you shall not escape me with your life. This is not the law of the hunt — what you have done to me today. Therefore I shall deprive you of your life, O dweller of the mountain."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ pāṇḍaveyena kirātaḥ prahasann iva uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā pāṇḍavaṃ savyasācinam
english: Thus addressed by the son of Pāṇḍu, the Kirata, as if laughing, spoke in a soft voice to Savyasācin, that Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: mamaivāyaṃ lakṣyabhūtaḥ pūrvam eva parigrahaḥ mamaiva ca prahāreṇa jīvitād vyavaropitaḥ
english: "This was my target first — it was my quarry from the beginning, and it was by my blow alone that it was stripped of its life."

sanskrit: doṣān svān nārhase 'nyasmai vaktuṃ svabaladarpitaḥ abhiṣakto 'smi mandātman na me jīvan vimokṣyase
english: "You should not attribute your own faults to another, puffed up with your own strength. I am under a vow, O dull-witted one — you shall not escape from me alive."

sanskrit: sthiro bhavasva mokṣyāmi sāyakān aśanīn iva ghaṭasva parayā śaktyā muñca tvam api sāyakān
english: "Stand firm! I shall release arrows like thunderbolts upon you. Strive with all your might — you too release your arrows."

sanskrit: tatas tau tatra saṃrabdhau garjamānau muhur muhuḥ śarair āśīviṣākārais tatakṣāte parasparam
english: Then those two, both enraged, roaring again and again at each other, cut at one another with arrows resembling venomous serpents.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaḥ śaravarṣaṃ kirāte samavāsṛjat tat prasannena manasā pratijagrāha śaṃkaraḥ
english: Then Arjuna released a rain of arrows upon the Kirata, and Shankara (Śiva) received it with a serene and undisturbed mind.

sanskrit: muhūrtaṃ śaravarṣaṃ tat pratigṛhya pinākadhṛk akṣatena śarīreṇa tasthau girir ivācalaḥ
english: Having received that rain of arrows for a moment, the wielder of the Pināka bow stood with his body utterly unhurt, immovable as a mountain.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā bāṇavarṣaṃ tan moghībhūtaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ paramaṃ vismayaṃ cakre sādhu sādhv iti cābravīt
english: Seeing that rain of arrows rendered utterly fruitless, Dhanañjaya was filled with the greatest wonder and said, "Well done! Well done!"

sanskrit: aho 'yaṃ sukumārāṅgo himavacchikharālayaḥ gāṇḍīvamuktān nārācān pratigṛhṇāty avihvalaḥ
english: "Ah, this tender-limbed dweller of the Himalayan peaks receives iron arrows shot from the Gāṇḍīva bow without the slightest agitation!"

sanskrit: ko 'yaṃ devo bhavet sākṣād rudro yakṣaḥ sureśvaraḥ vidyate hi giriśreṣṭhe tridaśānāṃ samāgamaḥ
english: "Who can this be in person — a god, Rudra, a yaksha, or the lord of the gods? For on this best of mountains there is an assembly of the thirty gods."

sanskrit: na hi madbāṇajālānām utsṛṣṭānāṃ sahasraśaḥ śakto 'nyaḥ sahituṃ vegam ṛte devaṃ pinākinam
english: "Truly, none other is capable of withstanding the force of my showers of arrows released by the thousands, except the god who holds the Pināka bow."

sanskrit: devo vā yadi vā yakṣo rudrād anyo vyavasthitaḥ aham enaṃ śarais tīkṣṇair nayāmi yamasādanam
english: "Whether this be a god or a yaksha, someone stationed here other than Rudra — I shall send him to the abode of Yama with my sharp arrows."

sanskrit: tato hṛṣṭamanā jiṣṇur nārācān marmabhedinaḥ vyasṛjac chatadhā rājan mayūkhān iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Then Jiṣṇu, with a joyful heart, released by the hundreds iron arrows that could pierce vital spots, O king, like the sun sending forth its rays.

sanskrit: tān prasannena manasā bhagavāṃl lokabhāvanaḥ śūlapāṇiḥ pratyagṛhṇāc chilāvarṣam ivācalaḥ
english: The blessed Lord, sustainer of the worlds, the trident-bearer, received all of them with a calm mind, like a mountain receiving a shower of stones.

sanskrit: kṣaṇena kṣīṇabāṇo 'tha saṃvṛttaḥ phalgunas tadā vitrāsaṃ ca jagāmātha taṃ dṛṣṭvā śarasaṃkṣayam
english: In a moment Phalguna's arrows were exhausted; and then, seeing his supply of arrows depleted, he fell into fear.

sanskrit: cintayām āsa jiṣṇus tu bhagavantaṃ hutāśanam purastād akṣayau dattau tūṇau yenāsya khāṇḍave
english: Jiṣṇu then thought of the blessed fire-god Agni, who had formerly given him two inexhaustible quivers at the time of the Khandava forest fire.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu mokṣyāmi dhanuṣā yan me bāṇāḥ kṣayaṃ gatāḥ ayaṃ ca puruṣaḥ ko 'pi bāṇān grasati sarvaśaḥ
english: "What shall I do with my bow now that my arrows are exhausted? And this man — whoever he is — swallows up all my arrows completely."

sanskrit: aham enaṃ dhanuṣkoṭyā śūlāgreṇeva kuñjaram nayāmi daṇḍadhārasya yamasya sadanaṃ prati
english: "I shall send him to the abode of Yama, the wielder of the rod, with the tip of my bow, as one would drive an elephant with the point of a goad."

sanskrit: saṃprāyudhyad dhanuṣkoṭyā kaunteyaḥ paravīrahā tad apy asya dhanur divyaṃ jagrāsa girigocaraḥ
english: The son of Kuntī, that slayer of enemy heroes, then fought with the tip of his bow — but that divine bow was swallowed up too by the mountain-dweller.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno grastadhanuḥ khaḍgapāṇir atiṣṭhata yuddhasyāntam abhīpsan vai vegenābhijagāma tam
english: Then Arjuna, his bow having been swallowed, stood with sword in hand; desiring to bring the battle to an end, he charged at him with great speed.

sanskrit: tasya mūrdhni śitaṃ khaḍgam asaktaṃ parvateṣv api mumoca bhujavīryeṇa vikramya kurunandanaḥ tasya mūrdhānam āsādya paphālāsivaro hi saḥ
english: The joy of the Kurus, striding forward with the strength of his arms, brought down his sharp sword upon the head of that one — even that sword, which does not stick even in mountains, shattered upon reaching his head.

sanskrit: tato vṛkṣaiḥ śilābhiś ca yodhayām āsa phalgunaḥ yathā vṛkṣān mahākāyaḥ pratyagṛhṇād atho śilāḥ
english: Then Phalguna fought with trees and with rocks — but the great-bodied one received the trees and then the rocks without any harm.

sanskrit: kirātarūpī bhagavāṃs tataḥ pārtho mahābalaḥ muṣṭibhir vajrasaṃsparśair dhūmam utpādayan mukhe prajahāra durādharṣe kirātasamarūpiṇi
english: Then Pārtha, of great strength, struck the blessed Lord who wore the Kirata form — on the face of that one who was in the guise of a Kirata, who was difficult to assail — with his fists, whose touch was like that of the thunderbolt, raising smoke upon impact.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakrāśanisamair muṣṭibhir bhṛśadāruṇaiḥ kirātarūpī bhagavān ardayām āsa phalgunam
english: Then the blessed Lord, in the guise of a Kirata, tormented Phalguna with his own fists, which were dreadful and equal to the thunderbolt of Indra.

sanskrit: tataś caṭacaṭāśabdaḥ sughoraḥ samajāyata pāṇḍavasya ca muṣṭīnāṃ kirātasya ca yudhyataḥ
english: Then arose a loud and most terrible cracking sound from the fists of the Pāṇḍava and of the Kirata as they fought.

sanskrit: sumuhūrtaṃ mahad yuddham āsīt tal lomaharṣaṇam bhujaprahārasaṃyuktaṃ vṛtravāsavayor iva
english: For a good while there was that great battle, hair-raising and filled with blows of the arms, like the fight between Vṛtra and Vāsava (Indra).

sanskrit: jahārātha tato jiṣṇuḥ kirātam urasā balī pāṇḍavaṃ ca viceṣṭantaṃ kirāto 'py ahanad balāt
english: Then mighty Jiṣṇu seized the Kirata with his chest; and the Kirata, in turn, forcefully struck the struggling Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: tayor bhujaviniṣpeṣāt saṃgharṣeṇorasos tathā samajāyata gātreṣu pāvako 'ṅgāradhūmavān
english: From the crushing grip of their arms, and from the friction of their chests, fire with smoke and embers arose on their bodies.

sanskrit: tata enaṃ mahādevaḥ pīḍya gātraiḥ supīḍitam tejasā vyākramad roṣāc cetas tasya vimohayan
english: Then Mahādeva, squeezing him with his limbs and utterly crushing him, overpowered him with his divine energy, in his fury bewildering his mind.

sanskrit: tato nipīḍitair gātraiḥ piṇḍīkṛta ivābabhau phalguno gātrasaṃruddho devadevena bhārata
english: Then Phalguna, with his limbs crushed and his body compressed, appeared as if reduced to a lump, his body seized by the god of gods, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nirucchvāso 'bhavac caiva saṃniruddho mahātmanā tataḥ papāta saṃmūḍhas tataḥ prīto 'bhavad bhavaḥ
english: He became unable to breathe, utterly held down by the great-souled one, and then fell down in a stupor — and thereupon Bhava (Śiva) was pleased.

sanskrit: bhagavān uvāca bho bho phalguna tuṣṭo 'smi karmaṇāpratimena te śauryeṇānena dhṛtyā ca kṣatriyo nāsti te samaḥ
english: The Blessed One said: "Ho, ho, Phalguna! I am satisfied with your unmatched deed, with this valor of yours, and with your steadfastness. There is no kshatriya your equal."

sanskrit: samaṃ tejaś ca vīryaṃ ca mamādya tava cānagha prītas te 'haṃ mahābāho paśya māṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: "Equal today are your energy and valor and mine, O sinless one. I am pleased with you, O mighty-armed one — look upon me, O bull among men."

sanskrit: dadāni te viśālākṣa cakṣuḥ pūrvaṛṣir bhavān vijeṣyasi raṇe śatrūn api sarvān divaukasaḥ
english: "I shall grant you the divine eye, O wide-eyed one. You are an ancient seer. You will conquer all your enemies in battle, even the celestials who dwell in heaven."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato devaṃ mahādevaṃ giriśaṃ śūlapāṇinam dadarśa phalgunas tatra saha devyā mahādyutim
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Phalguna there beheld the god, the great god, the mountain-dweller, the trident-bearer, of great radiance, together with the goddess.

sanskrit: sa jānubhyāṃ mahīṃ gatvā śirasā praṇipatya ca prasādayām āsa haraṃ pārthaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: He, Pārtha the conqueror of enemy cities, went down on both knees to the ground and bowing his head, sought to propitiate Hara.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kapardin sarvabhūteśa bhaganetranipātana vyatikramaṃ me bhagavan kṣantum arhasi śaṃkara
english: Arjuna said: "O Kapardī (wearer of matted locks), lord of all beings, destroyer of Bhaga's eyes — O Blessed Lord, O Shankara, please forgive my transgression."

sanskrit: bhavagaddarśanākāṅkṣī prāpto 'smīmaṃ mahāgirim dayitaṃ tava deveśa tāpasālayam uttamam
english: "Longing for the sight of you, O Lord, I have come to this great mountain, this beloved and supreme abode of ascetics, O lord of the gods."

sanskrit: prasādaye tvāṃ bhagavan sarvabhūtanamaskṛta na me syād aparādho 'yaṃ mahādevātisāhasāt
english: "I entreat you, O Blessed One, worshipped by all beings. May this offence of mine, committed out of reckless boldness toward Mahādeva, not count as a transgression."

sanskrit: kṛto mayā yad ajñānād vimardo 'yaṃ tvayā saha śaraṇaṃ saṃprapannāya tat kṣamasvādya śaṃkara
english: "Whatever combat I have committed against you out of ignorance — forgive that today, O Shankara, for I have come to you as a refuge."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tam uvāca mahātejāḥ prahasya vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ pragṛhya ruciraṃ bāhuṃ kṣāntam ity eva phalgunam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The great-radiant one whose banner bears the bull, laughing, took hold of his lovely arm and said to Phalguna: "It is forgiven."

sanskrit: bhagavān uvāca naras tvaṃ pūrvadehe vai nārāyaṇasahāyavān badaryāṃ taptavān ugraṃ tapo varṣāyutān bahūn
english: The Blessed One said: "You are Nara in a former body, the companion of Nārāyaṇa. At Badarika you performed fierce austerities for many thousands of years."

sanskrit: tvayi vā paramaṃ tejo viṣṇau vā puruṣottame yuvābhyāṃ puruṣāgryābhyāṃ tejasā dhāryate jagat
english: "Whether it be in you or in Viṣṇu, the highest of persons — the world is sustained by the energy of you two, the foremost of men."

sanskrit: śakrābhiṣeke sumahad dhanur jaladanisvanam pragṛhya dānavāḥ śastās tvayā kṛṣṇena ca prabho
english: "At the consecration of Śakra (Indra), taking up a great bow whose sound was like the rumble of a thundercloud, the Dānavas were slain by you and by Kṛṣṇa, O lord."

sanskrit: etat tad eva gāṇḍīvaṃ tava pārtha karocitam māyām āsthāya yad grastaṃ mayā puruṣasattama tūṇau cāpy akṣayau bhūyas tava pārtha yathocitau
english: "This is indeed that very Gāṇḍīva, fit for your hand, O Pārtha — what I swallowed by resorting to illusion, O best of men. And also your two inexhaustible quivers are yours again, O Pārtha, as is proper."

sanskrit: prītimān asmi vai pārtha tava satyaparākrama gṛhāṇa varam asmattaḥ kāṅkṣitaṃ yan nararṣabha
english: "I am pleased indeed, O Pārtha, with your true valour. Accept from me whatever boon you desire, O bull among men."

sanskrit: na tvayā sadṛśaḥ kaś cit pumān martyeṣu mānada divi vā vidyate kṣatraṃ tvatpradhānam ariṃdama
english: "No man among mortals or in heaven is equal to you, O giver of honour; the warrior class has you as its foremost, O subduer of enemies."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca bhagavan dadāsi cen mahyaṃ kāmaṃ prītyā vṛṣadhvaja kāmaye divyam astraṃ tad ghoraṃ pāśupataṃ prabho
english: Arjuna said: "O Blessed One, if you grant me my wish with affection, O lord whose banner bears the bull, I desire that terrible divine weapon, the Pāśupata, O lord."

sanskrit: yat tad brahmaśiro nāma raudraṃ bhīmaparākramam yugānte dāruṇe prāpte kṛtsnaṃ saṃharate jagat
english: "That which is called Brahmaśiras, that weapon of Rudra of terrible power — which at the dreadful end of an age destroys the entire world."

sanskrit: daheyaṃ yena saṃgrāme dānavān rākṣasāṃs tathā bhūtāni ca piśācāṃś ca gandharvān atha pannagān
english: "With which I could burn in battle the Dānavas and the Rākṣasas, and also beings, Piśācas, Gandharvas, and serpents."

sanskrit: yataḥ śūlasahasrāṇi gadāś cograpradarśanāḥ śarāś cāśīviṣākārāḥ saṃbhavanty anumantritāḥ
english: "From which, when it is charged with incantations, thousands of spears, terrifying maces, and arrows resembling venomous serpents come forth."

sanskrit: yudhyeyaṃ yena bhīṣmeṇa droṇena ca kṛpeṇa ca sūtaputreṇa ca raṇe nityaṃ kaṭukabhāṣiṇā
english: "With which I could fight in battle against Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, and the son of a charioteer who always speaks harsh words."

sanskrit: eṣa me prathamaḥ kāmo bhagavan bhaganetrahan tvatprasādād vinirvṛttaḥ samarthaḥ syām ahaṃ yathā
english: "This is my foremost wish, O Blessed One, O destroyer of Bhaga's eyes — that through your grace I may become capable of accomplishing it."

sanskrit: bhagavān uvāca dadāni te 'straṃ dayitam ahaṃ pāśupataṃ mahat samartho dhāraṇe mokṣe saṃhāre cāpi pāṇḍava
english: The Blessed One said: "I grant you that beloved and great Pāśupata weapon — you who are capable of holding it, releasing it, and also of withdrawing it, O Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: naitad veda mahendro 'pi na yamo na ca yakṣarāṭ varuṇo vātha vā vāyuḥ kuto vetsyanti mānavāḥ
english: "Not even great Indra knows this weapon, nor Yama, nor the king of the Yakṣas, nor Varuṇa, nor even Vāyu — how then shall mortals know it?"

sanskrit: na tv etat sahasā pārtha moktavyaṃ puruṣe kva cit jagad vinirdahet sarvam alpatejasi pātitam
english: "But this must not be rashly released upon any person, O Pārtha — if discharged upon one of insufficient energy, it would burn the entire world."

sanskrit: avadhyo nāma nāsty asya trailokye sacarācare manasā cakṣuṣā vācā dhanuṣā ca nipātyate
english: "There is no being in the three worlds, moving or unmoving, that cannot be slain by it — it is discharged by thought, by sight, by speech, and by bow."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tac chrutvā tvaritaḥ pārthaḥ śucir bhūtvā samāhitaḥ upasaṃgṛhya viśveśam adhīṣveti ca so 'bravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this, the eager Pārtha, having purified himself and become composed, embraced the lord of the universe and said: "Teach me."

sanskrit: tatas tv adhyāpayām āsa sarahasya nivartanam tad astraṃ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhaṃ mūrtimantam ivāntakam
english: Then he taught that weapon — along with its secret method of withdrawal — to the best of the Pāṇḍavas, as though it were the embodied god of death.

sanskrit: upatasthe mahātmānaṃ yathā tryakṣam umāpatim pratijagrāha tac cāpi prītimān arjunas tadā
english: He attended upon that great-souled one as befits the three-eyed lord, the husband of Umā; and Arjuna, filled with joy, received it duly.

sanskrit: tataś cacāla pṛthivī saparvatavanadrumā sasāgaravanoddeśā sagrāmanagarākarā
english: Then the earth trembled, together with its mountains, forests, and trees, together with its oceans and forest-tracts, together with its villages, cities, and mines.

sanskrit: śaṅkhadundubhighoṣāś ca bherīṇāṃ ca sahasraśaḥ tasmin muhūrte saṃprāpte nirghātaś ca mahān abhūt
english: The sounds of conches, kettledrums, and thousands of war-drums arose, and at that moment a great thunderclap occurred.

sanskrit: athāstraṃ jājvalad ghoraṃ pāṇḍavasyāmitaujasaḥ mūrtimad viṣṭhitaṃ pārśve dadṛśur devadānavāḥ
english: Then the gods and Dānavas beheld that terrible, blazing weapon standing in embodied form at the side of the Pāṇḍava of boundless energy.

sanskrit: spṛṣṭasya ca tryambakena phalgunasyāmitaujasaḥ yat kiṃ cid aśubhaṃ dehe tat sarvaṃ nāśam eyivat
english: And whatever inauspicious thing existed in the body of Phalguna of boundless energy, having been touched by the three-eyed one — all of it was annihilated.

sanskrit: svargaṃ gacchety anujñātas tryambakena tadārjunaḥ praṇamya śirasā pārthaḥ prāñjalir devam aikṣata
english: Then Arjuna, permitted by the three-eyed one with the words "Go to heaven," bowed his head and gazed upon the god with joined palms, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhus tridivanivāsināṃ vaśī; mahāmatir giriśa umāpatiḥ śivaḥ dhanur mahad ditijapiśācasūdanaṃ; dadau bhavaḥ puruṣavarāya gāṇḍivam
english: Then the lord, the sovereign of the dwellers of the three heavens, the great-minded Giriśa, the husband of Umā, the auspicious Śiva, Bhava — gave back the great bow Gāṇḍīva, the destroyer of Diti's sons and of Piśācas, to that best of men.

sanskrit: tataḥ śubhaṃ girivaram īśvaras tadā; sahomayā sitataṭasānukandaram vihāya taṃ patagamaharṣisevitaṃ; jagāma khaṃ puruṣavarasya paśyataḥ
english: Then the lord, the auspicious Ishvara, along with Umā, departing from that best of mountains — with its white slopes, ridges, and valleys, frequented by birds and sages — ascended into the sky as that best of men watched.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya saṃpaśyatas tv eva pinākī vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ jagāmādarśanaṃ bhānur lokasyevāstam eyivān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Even as he watched, the bearer of the Pināka bow, whose banner bears the bull, passed beyond sight, like the sun setting for the world.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaḥ paraṃ cakre vismayaṃ paravīrahā mayā sākṣān mahādevo dṛṣṭa ity eva bhārata
english: Then Arjuna, the slayer of enemy heroes, felt the utmost wonder, thinking: "By me, Mahādeva has been seen face to face" — thus, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: dhanyo 'smy anugṛhīto 'smi yan mayā tryambako haraḥ pinākī varado rūpī dṛṣṭaḥ spṛṣṭaś ca pāṇinā
english: "I am fortunate, I am blessed — for by me the three-eyed Hara, the bearer of the Pināka, the boon-giver, who had assumed a visible form, has been both seen and touched with my hand."

sanskrit: kṛtārthaṃ cāvagacchāmi param ātmānam ātmanā śatrūṃś ca vijitān sarvān nirvṛttaṃ ca prayojanam
english: "And I consider my purpose fulfilled, my highest self satisfied within myself, all my enemies conquered, and my mission accomplished."

sanskrit: tato vaiḍūryavarṇābho bhāsayan sarvato diśaḥ yādogaṇavṛtaḥ śrīmān ājagāma jaleśvaraḥ
english: Then the glorious lord of the waters, blazing with the hue of lapis lazuli, illuminating all directions, surrounded by hosts of aquatic beings, came there.

sanskrit: nāgair nadair nadībhiś ca daityaiḥ sādhyaiś ca daivataiḥ varuṇo yādasāṃ bhartā vaśī taṃ deśam āgamat
english: Varuṇa, lord and sovereign of the water-creatures, accompanied by nagas, rivers, streams, Daityas, Sādhyas, and divine beings, came to that place.

sanskrit: atha jāmbūnadavapur vimānena mahārciṣā kuberaḥ samanuprāpto yakṣair anugataḥ prabhuḥ
english: Then Kubera, the lord, whose body was of the colour of gold, arrived on his celestial car blazing with great radiance, followed by his Yakṣas.

sanskrit: vidyotayann ivākāśam adbhutopamadarśanaḥ dhanānām īśvaraḥ śrīmān arjunaṃ draṣṭum āgataḥ
english: As if illuminating the sky, of wondrous and incomparable appearance, the glorious lord of wealth came in order to see Arjuna.

sanskrit: tathā lokāntakṛc chrīmān yamaḥ sākṣāt pratāpavān mūrty amūrtidharaiḥ sārdhaṃ pitṛbhir lokabhāvanaiḥ
english: And likewise the glorious Yama himself, the destroyer of worlds, the powerful one, came together with the ancestral Pitṛs who sustain the worlds — some in bodily form and some without bodies.
